installs: Four skill directories under skills/, each holding one SKILL.md: second-brain (an onboarding wizard), second-brain-ingest, second-brain-query, and second-brain-lint. The onboarding skill also bundles six reference documents under skills/second-brain/references/ (agent-config templates for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI, a tooling guide, and the wiki schema) and one script, scripts/onboarding.sh, with a shell test beside it under tests/. The README installs the whole pack with npx skills add NicholasSpisak/second-brain and names Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI as hosts, which are the four the agent-config templates cover; it also says 40+ other Agent Skills hosts work, which is a format compatibility list rather than a documented install and is not recorded. Two further documents, docs/llm-wiki.md and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, describe the pattern and are not installed into a host.
distribution_machinery: skills/second-brain/scripts/onboarding.sh, which the onboarding skill tells the host to run once: it creates the vault's raw/, wiki/, and output/ directories, writes an empty wiki/index.md and wiki/log.md if they do not exist, reports whether three optional command-line tools are installed, and prints a JSON summary. It is idempotent scaffolding that reads nothing back and runs nothing at a later turn; tests/test_onboarding.sh exercises it.
not_a_system: Owns no state it reads back and does no enforced work: the wiki, its index, and its operation log are written and re-read by the host agent following the skill documents, and the only shipped code scaffolds the vault once at setup. The published second-brain project record is a different system with the same repository name, separated under ADR 020 by its own SQLite-backed store, terminal, web, and API surfaces, and container execution, none of which this pack has.
